title: Two polar splices in DOISST v2.1 (2005 ice input, 2016 ice-to-SST method) remove the 2005-2025 Arctic summer SST warming and make false post-2016 cold-spell rises poleward of 60 degrees
abstract: NOAA DOISST v2.1 is the standard daily SST record for marine heatwave (MHW) and cold-spell (MCS) studies. Earlier campaign work found input-change steps only at 60S-60N. We tested the two documented polar changes. (1) On 2005-01-01 the ice input changes from NASA GSFC to NCEP. On that day the DOISST ice extent (>=15%) increases by 1.11 million km2 (north) and 1.48 million km2 (south) relative to the NSIDC Sea Ice Index; ERA5 ice has no step. The excess grows later. The DOISST ice field gives 1982-2025 annual extent trends of -0.10 (Arctic; NSIDC -0.52) and +0.75 million km2 per decade (Antarctic; NSIDC -0.11). (2) On 2016-01-01 v2.1 starts a freezing-point ice-to-SST conversion; earlier data are identical to v2.0. NCEI produced v2.0 to April 2020, which gives a direct counterfactual for 1,578 days. Poleward of 60N, v2.1 minus v2.0 is -0.43 C in July and -1.34 C in cells with 35-50% ice; 37% of the July-September offset is in cells where only DOISST has ice. We removed this splice with a cell, month and ice-state offset. Poleward of 60N, the 2005-2025 July-September SST trend is +0.06 +/- 0.08 C per decade in published DOISST, +0.27 +/- 0.08 after the correction and +0.27 +/- 0.07 in ERA5. Published DOISST doubles the Arctic cold-spell days after 2016 (28.8 to 61.7 days per year) and raises them 2.5-fold in the Antarctic (40 to 101). With the correction they stay at 30.7 (Arctic) or fall to 24.9 (Antarctic); ERA5 shows no rise. The Arctic MHW intensity rise of 2007 (Huang et al. 2021) is also in ERA5 before its own input change, so it is not a DOISST artifact; the splice mainly lowers the recent MHW area cover. At 60S-60N v2.1 is 0.09 C warmer than v2.0 after 2016, but at 102 moored buoys v2.1 has no step (median -0.007 C, 95% interval -0.015 to 0.006); v2.0 drifted cold. Limitations: ERA5 is not truth and has its own 2007 step; the correction removes only the mean offset and returns 2016-2025 to the v2.0 method, which NOAA considers warm-biased in ice; the 2005 ice step is not corrected; no polar in situ SST and no CCI data were used. The bundle includes the correction field for |latitude| >= 50.
